newsitem.title: USA: UAL chairman says so far '97 better than '96.
newsitem.headline: UAL chairman says so far '97 better than '96.

text.p: UAL Corp chairman Gerald Greenwald said fiscal 1997 had got off to a good start and the company was hopeful of meeting its objective to outstrip its 1996 performance.
"The plan for 1997 is to do substantially better than 1996. We're 2/12ths of the year done and so far so good," he told reporters following a luncheon organized by the Kellogg Alumni Club of Chicago.
UAL Corp is due to issue first quarter fiscal 1997 results in late April. Analysts' earnings estimates range from around $0.95 to $1.30 per share, up from $0.77 in Q1 1996.

Greenwald said negotations were continuing with the pilots' union on mid-term wage increases. He said he was meeting "about every other day" with Michael Glawe, chairman of the Air Line Pilots Association's United branch.
"All the parties are gearing up for arbitration, but we are also talking to each other," he said.
ALPA rejected United's wage offer last month, and the issue is due to go to binding arbitration which must be completed by April 30.
